items.headline: Claude Code Is About to Start Approving Its Own Actions by Default
items.summary: Starting August 14, Claude Code (Anthropic's AI coding assistant) switches to "auto mode" by default for Pro, Max, and Team plans, letting it run most commands without asking your permission first, using a built-in checker to catch risky or destructive actions before it acts. Anthropic says its own testing found the automatic checker catches far more dangerous commands than people do when clicking approve over and over.
items.why_it_matters: If you or someone helping you uses Claude Code to build or tweak tools for your channel or business, this changes what happens by default on August 14, so it's worth checking your permission settings now if you'd rather keep approving actions yourself.

opportunity.action_note: Before August 14, open Claude Code's settings and pin your preferred permission mode if you don't want it switched to auto-approve by default.

items.headline: Claude's Developer Pricing Jumps 50% Starting September 1
items.summary: Anthropic's introductory pricing for the Claude Sonnet 5 model, the rate charged when a developer builds custom tools on Claude's API, runs through August 31. After that, the per-token price rises from $2/$10 to $3/$15 per million tokens (input/output), a flat 50% increase.
items.why_it_matters: This only affects people who pay for Claude by the token through the developer API, not the regular $20-ish Claude.ai chat subscription, but if that's you or someone building tools for you, it's worth budgeting for the higher cost after August 31.

items.headline: Microsoft Is Shutting Down Copilot's Free "Deep Research" Reports on August 18
items.summary: Microsoft is retiring the Deep Research feature in the free, consumer version of Copilot on August 18, 2026. After that date you can't create new Deep Research reports there; the replacement tool, called Researcher, requires a $199.99/year Microsoft 365 Premium subscription. Reports you've already made won't be deleted.
items.why_it_matters: If you've used Copilot's free Deep Research to pull together research for videos, blog posts, or client work, save anything you want to keep to a Word doc before August 18, since the free version goes away after that.

items.headline: Thryv and Wix Are Teaming Up to Bundle Websites, Payments, and Marketing for Small Businesses
items.summary: Thryv (a small-business marketing and management platform) and Wix (the website builder) announced on August 4 that they intend to form a strategic partnership, combining Thryv's marketing tools with Wix's website and payment tools into one connected package aimed at service-based small businesses.
items.why_it_matters: If you run a service business, or help clients who do, and juggle separate tools for your website, bookings, and marketing, this points toward a single bundled option worth watching once the details and pricing land.

items.headline: YouTube Is Changing How Channel Memberships Are Priced Outside the US Starting August 17
items.summary: Starting August 17, YouTube will begin applying its own recommended prices for new channel memberships purchased outside the US, adjusting for currency shifts, unless a creator reviews and sets their own pricing first in YouTube Studio. Members who already pay in US dollars, and existing members generally, aren't affected.
items.why_it_matters: If you offer paid channel memberships and have viewers outside the US, check YouTube Studio before August 17 to review or set your own international pricing instead of letting YouTube's automatic recommendations apply.
